From e4500d7525f9223a0a46431caa6d0f2d165f05ce Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@linaro.org>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2024 11:25:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] bus: stm32_firewall: fix off by one in
 stm32_firewall_get_firewall()

The "nb_firewall" variable is the number of elements in the firewall[]
array, which is allocated in stm32_firewall_populate_bus().  So change
this > comparison to >= to prevent an out of bound access.

Fixes: 5c9668cfc6d7 ("firewall: introduce stm32_firewall framework")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@linaro.org>
Reviewed-by: Gatien Chevallier <gatien.chevallier@foss.st.com>
Signed-off-by: Alexandre Torgue <alexandre.torgue@foss.st.com>

diff --git a/drivers/bus/stm32_firewall.c b/drivers/bus/stm32_firewall.c
index decb79449047..2fc9761dadec 100644
--- a/drivers/bus/stm32_firewall.c
+++ b/drivers/bus/stm32_firewall.c
@@ -53,7 +53,7 @@ int stm32_firewall_get_firewall(struct device_node *np, struct stm32_firewall *f
 			return err;
 		}
 
-		if (j > nb_firewall) {
+		if (j >= nb_firewall) {
 			pr_err("Too many firewall controllers");
 			of_node_put(provider);
 			return -EINVAL;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/bus/stm32_firewall.c`**
- The conditional check in the `stm32_firewall_get_firewall` function was modified from `if (j > nb_firewall)` to `if (j >= nb_firewall)`. This change ensures that the comparison correctly prevents an out-of-bounds access to the `firewall[]` array by allowing the index `j` to be equal to `nb_firewall`, which represents the number of elements in the array.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug related to array bounds in the `stm32_firewall_get_firewall` function. The original condition could lead to accessing an invalid index of the `firewall[]` array, potentially causing undefined behavior. By changing the comparison operator from `>` to `>=`, the patch ensures that the function correctly handles the maximum valid index, thus fixing the off-by-one error. This change is directly linked to the allocation of the `firewall[]` array in the `stm32_firewall_populate_bus()` function, where `nb_firewall` is defined.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (j > nb_firewall) {
```
Reason:
The condition `j > nb_firewall` allows `j` to exceed the valid index range of the `firewall[]` array, which has indices from `0` to `nb_firewall - 1`. If `j` equals `nb_firewall`, it results in an out-of-bounds access, leading to undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (j >= nb_firewall) {
```
Reason:
Changing the condition to `j >= nb_firewall` ensures that the code checks for both the case where `j` is equal to `nb_firewall` and when it exceeds it. This prevents any out-of-bounds access to the `firewall[]` array, thus maintaining safe memory access.
